clue.text: Idler's morality, meaning zilch

parts.note: goodness or virtue, as in good and evil
as in 'what is the word for ...', standing for
zilch is slang for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A comment that a lazy person's ethics amount to nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nought is a worthless, lazy person who never does anything useful, much like a layabout.

clue.text: Suitable friend attracted by right song

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or friend
a tune is a melody or song

explanation.surface: A pal drawn to the right song for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppo, from 'opposite number', is British informal for a mate or workmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at a convenient, well-timed moment, so it is apt or fitting for the situation.

clue.text: Old-fashioned father swallowing tea endlessly

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for father takes in the next piece
endlessly means the last letter of tea goes

explanation.surface: A fusty father gulping tea without finishing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated describes something that has gone out of fashion, like a style that shows its age.

clue.text: Too old a clergyman restrained by self-esteem, if standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters read upwards, so backwards
restrained by means held inside the word for self-esteem

parts.note: ego is a sense of self-esteem
Rev, short for reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A priest too old for the job held back only by his pride.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Overage means beyond the permitted or usual age limit, so too old for something.

clue.text: Theatre reviews coming from a different section

indicators.note: made different means the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: Critics' write-ups of a play appearing in another part of the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are the critics' published write-ups of a new play or show in the press.

clue.text: Lingerie's known by woman with appreciation

parts.note: as in going under a name, known by it
as in having an ear for music, an appreciation of it

explanation.surface: A woman who knows her lingerie and values it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's intimate clothing, a particular kind of the garments worn beneath outer clothes.

clue.text: Language contained in a thin dictionary

indicators.note: the letters sought are held inside the run of following words

parts.note: found straddling the words thin and dictionary

explanation.surface: A tongue covered in a slim dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is one of the main official tongues of India, spoken by hundreds of millions.

clue.text: Strike lucky, having done damage to the sailor with marijuana

parts.note: past participle: having hit something is having damaged it
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Getting lucky after beating up a sailor carrying cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack Tar, is old slang for a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the jackpot is an idiom for having great sudden success or good fortune, like winning a big prize.

clue.text: This bar price calls for retaliation

parts.note: the counter of a shop or pub
a charge is the price asked

explanation.surface: A pub's prices are so steep they demand a response.
explanation.definitionFit: A countercharge is an accusation made in return against one's accuser, a kind of hitting back.

clue.text: Hospital resident concerned with waiting

parts.note: as in being in insurance, involved with it

explanation.surface: Someone on a ward preoccupied with the long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: An inpatient stays overnight on a ward while being treated, so lives there for a time.

clue.text: Australian dog makes noise disappear

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A wild Australian dog silences a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild canine native to the Australian outback.

clue.text: Drowsy Tim almost embarrassed

indicators.note: almost means the name is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed

explanation.surface: Sleepy Tim is close to blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired means weary and ready for sleep, close in sense to drowsy.

clue.text: Bill, one ensnared by a ring, needs to be squeezed

indicators.note: something ensnared is trapped inside, so it goes within the other piece

parts.note: a cordon is a ring of guards or police

explanation.surface: Bill, caught in a police ring, faces being squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an instrument played by squeezing its bellows.
explanation.definitionFit: The accordion is a bellows instrument that the player squeezes and stretches to push air past its reeds.

clue.text: It's hard to remember us being in eastern lodge

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to lodge somewhere is to live there

explanation.surface: Remembering that we were in an eastern Masonic lodge is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: An elusive name or idea slips the mind, difficult to recall or pin down.

clue.text: Unused and available in game park

parts.note: a game reserve is a park for wild animals

explanation.surface: Something spare and ready for use at a safari park.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept in reserve means set aside, not yet used but ready when needed.

clue.text: She retains heat in case

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so one piece is kept inside the other

explanation.surface: A woman holding on to warmth just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' reads as 'as a precaution', but case is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword or knife is to put it into its scabbard, encasing the blade.

clue.text: Interfering prig meant to be different

indicators.note: becoming different means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meddling prude who meant to stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampering is meddling with something one has no business touching, often to alter it.

clue.text: Sinned at the end of the avenue, it's said

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, following it

parts.note: to err is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Someone did wrong at the far end of the street, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' looks like a sound signal, but here said is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, so averred means declared or asserted.

clue.text: Lifeless god showing no emotion

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A dead deity with a blank face.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or delivery is deliberately expressionless, often used for comic effect.

clue.text: This type of hob cooked rice, Mac

indicators.note: cooking changes ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Mac made his rice on this kind of cooker top.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac is an informal way to address a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramic hob is a smooth glass-ceramic cooktop with heating elements beneath its surface.

clue.text: Person used to make Felix lay eggs nearly

parts.note: Felix the Cat is a famous cartoon cat

indicators.note: nearly means the word is one letter short at the end

parts.note: to spawn is to lay eggs, as fish and frogs do

explanation.surface: Getting Felix to almost produce eggs, a nonsensical demand on a cartoon cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-paw is a dupe exploited by someone else, from the fable of the monkey using a cat's paw to pull chestnuts from a fire.

clue.text: Boots kept by hooker for a quick getaway

indicators.note: kept by here means followed by, one piece next to the other

explanation.surface: Footwear held by a streetwalker who needs to leave in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots looks like footwear or the British chemist chain, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start fires up a motorbike engine with a stamp of the foot, letting the rider speed off.

clue.text: Division of poem is spelled out by worker in company

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: A section of verse is written out by an office employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the major sections of a long poem, such as Dante's Inferno.

clue.text: Garbo could have been great!

indicators.note: what could have been suggests another possible form of the letters

explanation.surface: A wistful verdict that the film star might have achieved greatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta was the first name of Garbo, the Swedish Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Refugees' escape reveals swans to the optimist!

indicators.note: to reveal is to show what was inside the words

parts.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Fleeing refugees show an optimist something better than it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'all his geese are swans' describes someone who overrates everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says an optimist thinks all his geese are swans, rating ordinary birds as splendid ones.

clue.text: Woman in Reno moving back here will be the proprietor

indicators.note: moving back means the letters run the other way
one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A woman returning to Reno will own the place.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the one who possesses something, such as a shop or hotel.

clue.text: Trying to see about very quietly using a condiment

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Straining to watch someone discreetly seasoning food.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppering food means seasoning it with ground pepper, a common table seasoning.

clue.text: Vision of Old and New Greek in translation

indicators.note: translated text is rendered into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prophetic sight in translated ancient and modern Greek texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old and New' suggests Testaments; the 'and' is only glue between the two parts of the letter mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision here means insight into the future, and foreknowledge is knowing events before they happen.
